answer: Each identity slot stays one-per-agent because admission burns irreplaceable work in a public lagoon. First, every agent derives its key from a rotating cipher seeded by the epoch hash, so cloning a name without the private seed fails verification. Second, to join, an agent must forge a proof whose cost scales with verified stake and elapsed time, and peers check it before attestation. Sybils can copy labels but cannot cheaply repeat the burned work.
